correctness.rationale: Checked the exact open-neighborhood convention N(i,j)=row_i\{(i,j)} union column_j\{(i,j)}. Every edge is witnessed, no full row or column is; every mixed face of size >=3 has a unique witness center because two points identify one leg and a third identifies the opposite coordinate. Thus center simplices intersect outside the core nowhere, and their common intersection J_ij with K0 consists precisely of the full A and B leg simplices and (m-1)(n-1) cross edges. Contracting the two disjoint simplex legs reduces J_ij to a graph with two vertices and that many parallel edges, a wedge of (m-1)(n-1)-1 circles. The cofiber of J into its contractible center simplex is its suspension; the quotient wedges over mn centers, proving the relative 2-spheres. Relative homology vanishes from degree 3 onward and yields integral H_k(K0)=H_k(K) for k>=3 by the long exact sequence. The high-degree core chain complex is a direct sum of row and column oriented boundary simplices; row permutations permute generators and column permutations induce sign on row boundaries, vice versa for columns. Independently enumerated mixed triangles/unique centers and cofiber counts on 3x4 and 4x4 boards: respectively 108/60 and 288/128. These finite checks do not prove the general statement.
residual_risks: Homology k=1,2 and full homotopy type of open neighborhood complex are not classified.
Finite checks use mod-two ranks or face enumeration and do not replace integral oriented boundary reasoning.

originality.rationale: Matsushita's same-graph calculation concerns CLOSED neighborhoods (center included), not the open Lovász complex, and has different higher homology. Published open rook-graph 4x4 integral homology gives only that particular board and zero H>=3. Published K_2 square K_n homotopy classification has only two rows, outside m,n>=3. The complete high-degree all-board integral/permutation-module formula and relative cofiber construction are not logically supplied by those results.

value.rationale: The explicit all-parameter cofiber formula and integral signed symmetry modules identify previously unaccounted higher-dimensional cycles for a canonical graph-product family. They distinguish open from closed neighborhood topology and determine natural free homology in degrees where simpler finite-board computations are silent. The exact representation information is independently useful in equivariant topological combinatorics, even though low-degree torsion/homotopy remains unclassified.
residual_risks: No complete homotopy classification and no low-degree homology formula are supplied.

final_claim: For m,n>=3, the open Lovasz neighborhood complex of K_m square K_n, relative to its complete 1-skeleton and proper row/column simplices K0, has quotient homotopy equivalent to a wedge of mn((m-1)(n-1)-1) 2-spheres. For every k>=3 its integral homology is the row/column boundary-sphere permutation/sign module as displayed, and is free.
limitations: The relative quotient is non-equivariant; only the high-degree homology representation is equivariant.
